extraction_warnings: This paper reports aggregate study-level data and does not provide individual subject or sample identifiers. The samples array contains a single record representing the study cohort as a whole, not individual per-sample rows. Sample-level metadata (subject_id, sample_id, individual sex, age, disease status) are not available in this paper.
Age information is provided only as a range (23–34 years) at study level, not per individual sample.
Sex/gender distribution is reported as an aggregate (74% female, 26% male) but not linked to individual samples.

The paper distinguishes between two travel destination subgroups (Central Africa n=17, Indian peninsula n=18) at the results level, but does not provide sample-level identifiers or mappings to individual subjects.
Control classification is marked 'Not Used' because all subjects were travelers (cases); no control group was included in this travel-acquisition study design.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Study is observational and focuses on antibiotic resistance gene acquisition during travel; it is not a clinical trial with treatment outcomes.
No individual-level demographic data (smoking, reproductive status, HLA) extracted; schema fields match study-level population description (23-34 years old, 74% female, health care students).
Antimalarial use is reported as aggregate data, not per-participant; detailed drug names/dosages not consistently provided across all 35 subjects.
